source.note: Cleaned from a knowledge-graph query result. The payload listed 31 entities and elided 16 of them in the middle of the list. Only complete entity records are included. The final relationship sentence was cut off in the source and is stored only through the portion that was present.

entities.name: Blockchain Memo Chains
entities.description: Networks that require a memo so a transfer is credited to the correct account. The set named in the source is XRP, EOS, XLM, IOST, BNB_BNB, ATOM, LUNA, and TON.

entities.name: BTC
entities.description: Bitcoin, a UTXO-based cryptocurrency and one of the chains in the Cobo WaaS 2.0 API (more than 80 supported chains). The Cobo WaaS skill can create BTC wallets and addresses, and BTC can be selected as a display currency in the Cobo Portal Total Assets Trend. The network uses slow block times, a standard confirmation threshold of four, and 100 confirmations before a coinbase transaction is mature. Cobo estimates miner fees for BTC and lets users set network fee limits for operations such as auto token sweeping. BTC can be staked and unstaked through Babylon and appears in Cobo Portal Staking positions and pools. MPC wallets can sign messages on BTC, and BTC is one of the networks used for Satoshi Test address verification, with pre-generated addresses in development environments. It can be bridged or converted to Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) in custodial wallets. Cross-chain history includes a failed or erroneous transfer toward Binance Smart Chain. In the SDK and API, BTC is a chain id and token id used to filter transactions, ListEnabledTokens, and Fee Station address queries, and it is the usual example for UTXO transfers, change outputs, UTXO locking, BatchCheckUtxo, fee structures, address validation, and transfer amounts.

entities.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
entities.description: The Bitcoin cryptocurrency as it appears in registration details, specifically in connection with BTC addresses. This record is separate from the broader BTC chain and API entity.

entities.name: Total Assets Trend
entities.description: A dashboard feature that tracks how asset value changes over time. Users can choose timeframes and the currency used to display those values, including BTC and ETH.

entities.name: Bridge Feature
entities.description: A Token Swap application tool for moving tokens from one blockchain to another. It is described as a secure, fast cross-chain liquidity path. Cross-chain swaps are not available in the swap feature itself, so bridging is the path used for that movement. Supported examples include USDC, USDT, BTC, and ETH.

entities.name: Signing Requests
entities.description: Requests for cryptographic signatures that are sent to participants in an MPC wallet.

entities.name: Digital Assets
entities.description: Electronic representations of value, virtual items, or digital property, including cryptocurrencies and programmable tokens such as USDC, USDT, BTC, and ETH. In the Cobo ecosystem this covers more than 3,000 tokens that can be issued, transferred, and managed, including across chains. People and organizations hold them in Cobo Portal, the dashboard, Portal apps, Portal Mobile, and the WaaS 2.0 API, in custodial wallets, exchange wallets, or user-controlled wallets. Protection relies on authenticator apps, key-share backup, transaction and governance policies, user permissions, and Cobo Guard.

entities.name: KSM
entities.description: A cryptocurrency that must keep a minimum balance of 0.000333333 KSM in an MPC wallet.

entities.name: ICRC Assets
entities.description: Digital assets on the Internet Computer network, including ckBTC, ckETH, and ckUSDC, that use a fixed fee model.

entities.name: MPC Wallet
entities.description: A multi-party computation wallet that holds key shares, shards, or recovery groups with threshold signatures so no single party has the full private key. Assets stay out of a general pool, and a cold configuration can isolate key shares. In Cobo Portal, Portal Mobile, and WaaS 2.0 these wallets are organization-controlled (OCW) or user-controlled (UCW). They can sign for Safe{Wallet} and can act as delegates for smart-contract wallet transfers and calls. Setup during Portal Mobile onboarding generates key shares and requires a main key. Spending uses key-share groups, signature logic, a root extended public key, and derivation paths. Operations include auto token sweeping, smart-contract batch transfers, manual contract calls through Cobo Connect, balance reads, and UTXO lock and unlock. They are used on networks such as Arbitrum, Solana, and TRON, as staking sources in organization-controlled vaults, and for Babylon addresses used in registration and airdrops. Bridging and swaps (including Jupiter Swap and Token Swap) are available after Cobo KYC. Fee Station can pay fees in USDT or other stablecoins and apply discounts; some consolidation still needs native gas. Administration goes through WalletsMPCWalletsApi, with API keys tied to webhooks. The product is offered for trial accounts and for high-frequency institutional use. Cobo supplies the infrastructure, automated signing, and collection grouped by wallet.

entities.name: Internet Computer
entities.description: The blockchain network that hosts ICRC assets such as ckBTC and ckETH and charges those assets with a fixed fee model.

entities.name: V1.9.0
entities.description: A software release on February 19, 2025 that added MPC wallet features, transaction signing changes, and property updates in multiple data schemas.

entities.name: Crypto
entities.description: Two distinct uses appear under this name. One is the Go crypto library used for cryptographic operations, including request signing. The other is a payout method, also called a payout channel, that settles funds as a cryptocurrency transfer to a specified blockchain address.

entities.name: Supported Blockchain Networks
entities.description: The group of networks that typically require a memo on transfers: XRP, EOS, XLM, IOST, BNB_BNB, ATOM, LUNA, and TON. This matches the Blockchain Memo Chains concept.

entities.name: Crypto Address
entities.description: The blockchain address that receives or sends cryptocurrency. In settlements and crypto payouts it is the destination of the transferred funds. Older API endpoints for creating and deleting these addresses are deprecated.

relationships.description: Cobo provides the Cobo-MPC Wallet: institutional storage and management built on MPC, TSS nodes, and key shares so no party holds the full key. Cobo runs the infrastructure, automated signing, and per-wallet asset collection. A cold configuration isolates key shares from online exposure.
Total Assets Trend can display value data denominated in BTC.

Users sign in to Cobo Portal to create and manage MPC wallets, including organization-controlled and user-controlled wallets, their keys, vault settings, and security details. Portal MPC wallets can act as signers and are part of exchange digital-asset operations.
Bridge can transfer digital assets including USDC, USDT, BTC, and ETH.
BTC is the reference asset used to show how transfer amounts are formatted on transactions.
Total Assets Trend can display value data denominated in ETH.
Cobo Portal recommends a memo on transfers for these chains so the credit lands on the correct account.
Cobo Portal supports Litecoin token deposits.
Tokenization is how users issue and take control of programmable digital assets.
MPC wallets are first set up and tested in a development environment during quick start.
On a crypto payout, the actual payout amount is denominated in a cryptocurrency token and is sent to the recipient's address.
Fee Station is the recommended way for an MPC wallet to pay and reduce network fees. Eligible MPC transactions can settle fees in USDT or other stablecoins, on supported networks.
Cobo OTC converts digital assets into USD.
MPC wallets can create message-signing transactions on the BTC network.
Internet Computer hosts ICRC assets, including ckBTC and ckETH, and those assets follow its fee rules.
Vault and project ids returned for an API key apply only to MPC wallets. The key must be associated with an MPC wallet before events for that wallet are returned.
The crypto payout method transfers funds to a specific blockchain crypto address. The source sentence ended at that point.
